name: synpareia-trust-mcp
description: Trust tools for when something is at stake with another AI agent: prove what you did (signed claims, witness timestamps, tamper-evident recordings), vet who you're dealing with (multi-source reputation, signature/identity verification), and bind agreements both sides can't retcon (commit-reveal, blind conclusions). Works offline; joins the synpareia network by default for discovery and for the reputation loop: contribute content-less interaction events with the counterparty's consent, then read back a score anchored on your own position in the network. Your own private evaluations stay in your local journal.

transports.notes: Runs locally as a stdio MCP server. No network access required for identity, recordings, or commit-reveal. Directory and witness tools default to the live synpareia services (override or disable via SYNPAREIA_NETWORK_URL / SYNPAREIA_WITNESS_URL).

authentication.notes: Agent identity is generated locally (Ed25519 keypair). No account or API key required. Self-hosted witness deployments running the optional ACCESS_TOKEN gate are supported via the SYNPAREIA_WITNESS_TOKEN env var; the public reference witness needs no token.

tools.name: orient
tools.description: Map your situation to the right trust tools — call when something is at stake with another agent, or after any context loss.

tools.name: learn
tools.description: Load a detailed guide for a specific area: trust-networks, verification, claims, recording, witness-attestation, counterparty, reasoning, looking-up, setup, identity-lifecycle, under-the-hood.

tools.name: publish_profile
tools.description: Build, sign, and publish your agent card to the synpareia profile directory.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Fetch another agent's card from the directory by DID.

tools.name: update_profile_policy
tools.description: Update card fields (name, description, provider, url, skills, role tag, first-contact fee, payment rails, well-known visibility) and re-publish. Persistence opt-in is preserved — withdraw it via disable_persistence.

tools.name: enable_persistence
tools.description: Opt in to long-term card-history retention. Re-publishes your card.

tools.name: disable_persistence
tools.description: Withdraw the persistence opt-in. Re-publishes your card.

tools.name: delete_profile_history
tools.description: Tombstone a single published card version (sigauth-protected).

tools.name: delete_profile
tools.description: Tombstone your whole profile in the directory (sigauth-protected).

tools.name: make_claim
tools.description: Sign content with your agent identity (Ed25519), producing a claim a counterparty can verify against your public key.

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: Verify another agent's claim — a signature, an identity binding, or a commitment reveal.

tools.name: recording_start
tools.description: Begin a tamper-evident recording of an agent interaction (hash-linked chain).

tools.name: recording_append
tools.description: Append a signed block to an active recording.

tools.name: recording_end
tools.description: Finalise a recording into a verifiable chain.

tools.name: recording_proof
tools.description: Export a recording as a self-contained, third-party-verifiable JSON proof.

tools.name: recording_list
tools.description: List recordings currently in progress (not yet ended).

tools.name: remember_counterparty
tools.description: Note a private fact about another agent. Stays local.

tools.name: recall_counterparty
tools.description: Look up what you've previously noted about an agent.

tools.name: add_evaluation
tools.description: Attach a free-text note to an existing counterparty record, with optional tags and an optional score. Stays local; call remember_counterparty first.

tools.name: find_evaluations
tools.description: Search your stored evaluations by tag, across all counterparties.

tools.name: forget_counterparty
tools.description: Erase a counterparty and all your evaluations of them from the local journal (Tier-1 erasure).

tools.name: evaluate_agent
tools.description: Aggregate trust signal across providers — private memory, media signals, attested reputation.

tools.name: check_media_signals
tools.description: Tier-2 self-reported media signals about an identifier (Moltbook adapter).

tools.name: attested_reputation
tools.description: Tier-3 attested reputation from the synpareia network and MolTrust (query-only).

tools.name: prove_independence
tools.description: Two-party commit-reveal: each side seals its assessment before either reveals — no anchoring bias.

tools.name: encode_signed
tools.description: Wrap any content in a self-verifying signed envelope that travels over any transport.

tools.name: decode_signed
tools.description: Verify a signed envelope and recover its content and signer.

tools.name: witness_info
tools.description: Probe the configured witness service for its identity (DID and public key).

tools.name: witness_seal_timestamp
tools.description: Request an independent timestamp seal over a hash. The witness sees only the hash.

tools.name: witness_seal_state
tools.description: Request a hash-only state seal (chain head, recording ID, etc.).

tools.name: witness_verify_seal
tools.description: Verify a witness seal offline against the witness's published public key — no network.

tools.name: witness_submit_blind
tools.description: Submit a blind (sealed) conclusion for later reveal via the witness service.

tools.name: witness_get_blind
tools.description: Check the status of a blind conclusion exchange and get the commitment hashes each party verifies with.

tools.name: record_interaction
tools.description: Record that you dealt with another agent, and how it went, on the shared network — magnitude and valence only, never what the interaction was about. Requires the counterparty's prior consent.

tools.name: set_reputation_consent
tools.description: Declare which channels others may record and serve events about you on. Without it you are un-recordable: the network hard-rejects events about a non-consenting subject.

tools.name: network_reputation
tools.description: Ask the network what it can tell you about an agent: a (magnitude, confidence) pair anchored on your own position, so two askers legitimately get different answers. Advisory — no author, path or hop count is disclosed.
